newsitem.title: EGYPT: Egypt says had bought 400,000T Australia wheat.
newsitem.headline: Egypt says had bought 400,000T Australia wheat.

text.p: Egypt's main commodities buyer said on Wednesday that he bought 400,000 tonnes of soft white Australian wheat about 10 days ago, a deal which the Australian Wheat Board (AWB) denies.

Samir Shakankiri, vice chairman of the state's General Authority for Supply Commodities, told Reuters he bought the wheat while purchasing 500,000 tonnes of French wheat on February 1 and 2 at prices between $140.50 and $143.90 a tonne.
"We bought 400,000 tonnes of Australian wheat at the same time as we were buying the French wheat," he added, but did not say how much he had paid for the Australian wheat.
But AWB said in its weekly grain market report issued on February 10 that it had not sold wheat to Egypt in its 500,000 tonne tender and had sold to India instead.
Shakankiri said that both Australian and French wheat purchases would tide him over until late July at least.
"We have enough wheat to last well into the next financial year," he said. The Egyptian financial year begins on July 1.
